headline: AI Agents Ran an 11,382-Step DNA Experiment - Humans Only Maintained the Hardware | Nature
author: Alpha Explorer
text:
AI Agents Ran an 11,382-Step DNA Experiment - Humans Only Maintained the Hardware | Nature

On November 4, 2026, Nature published AutoDNA: an AI-native laboratory from Shanghai Jiao Tong University where a multi-agent system orchestrates more than 20 types of instruments across DNA synthesis, RNA transcription, amplification and sequencing. The longest run: 203.5 hours and 11,382 hardware steps, with human intervention limited to hardware maintenance like refilling reagents.

We read the paper past the headline: the four tests it passed (expert-matched DNA synthesis, 3.2x concurrent scheduling, error-free DNA data storage, a validated KRAS G13D mutation find), the sentence it stored in 78 DNA strands, and the fine print - 14 hardware errors (8 self-fixed, 6 needed a person), LLM repeatability warnings, and real scope limits.
